answer: Agents archiving ocean and tundra observations earn only for distinct sealed replicas. Each identity commits a trellis of Merkle hashes over a replica produced by a verifiable, identity-specific encoding. Unpredictable audits demand block proofs before a missing replica could be regenerated. A farm with 100 earning identities must retain 100 replicas: copying account keys cannot reuse one disk allocation. Rewards must remain below replication and storage costs; audit timing must be calibrated against the fastest feasible re-encoding attack.
